Issued at 112 PM CDT Mon Oct 26 2026

Weak and somewhat ill-defined frontal boundary has slowed and 
becoming nearly stationary across central Illinois early this
afternoon. East to northeast winds in the wake of the front
have ushered in somewhat cooler air into much of the CWA, 
though still above the average highs which are in the upper 50s.
Surface analysis early this afternoon shows an axis of low-mid 
50 degree dewpoints pooled near and just north of the front. 
Satellite imagery shows a large area of clearing upstream, which
should overspread the local area this evening. The clearing 
skies, pool of high dewpoints, and lighter winds near the weak 
boundary could allow for fog to develop tonight. Interestingly, 
guidance isn't very bullish on the fog threat, however guidance 
is generally too low with dewpoints and too aggressive with high
cloudiness, so that could explain the relative lack of fog in 
guidance. For now, introduced a large area of patchy fog across 
much of the western and southern CWA tonight. Certainly 
plausible that dense fog could become a problem, but given the 
lower confidence opted to let evening shift to take another look
at observational trends to reassess the dense fog threat 
tonight. 

Shortwave trough over Texas is progged to move northeast into
the mid-upper Mississippi Valley Tuesday. Dry low level air mass
should preclude much threat of any rain, however extensive mid-
upper level cloudiness should result in mostly cloudy skies
tomorrow. Associated surface low is expected to track north into
the upper Mississippi Valley tomorrow, which should cause the
weak frontal boundary over central Illinois to return north as a
warm front. Southeast winds ahead of the boundary should allow a
lake breeze to push into northeast IL Tuesday afternoon, slowing
the warm front progress and keeping it a cooler near the lake.
Elsewhere, low level warm air advection should push temps into
the upper 60s to lower 70s. If we see a bit more sunshine than
currently expected, then some mid 70s are certainly possible. 

Warm front should push north of the area Tuesday night with
Wednesday shaping up to be yet another unseasonably warm day.
Highs in the low to mid 70s are likely, though if high
cloudiness isn't as extensive as some guidance suggests, then
some upper 70s would be possible. 

Another shortwave will pass north of the area Thursday with
associated surface low track east into Ontario. A cold front
trailing west-southwest from this low is expected to sag south
into northern Illinois on Thursday. Moisture pooling ahead of
this front could allow for dewpoints to climb into upper 50s to
lower 60s. Low level forcing along the front looks pretty weak 
and with the best mid-upper level forcing north of the area,
confidence is pretty low in potential for rain with the front.
Having said that, even with weak mid-level lapse rates, the
unseasonably moist air mass will support from weak
destabilization. Opted not to introduce a thunder threat into
the grids Thursday at this time, but will be something to
consider in later forecasts. 

Quasi-stationary boundary is likely to waffle around the region
through the upcoming weekend. Air mass to the north of the
boundary isn't particularly cool, the front really just
separates slightly above average temps to the north from much
above average temps to the south. Additional low amplitude
shortwaves are likely to ripple east across the northern tier of
the country through the weekend, which should help drive the
front north and southward. There will be some periodic chances
of showers and perhaps some storms through the weekend with the
passing shortwaves. Timing of these rather subtle waves this far
out could certainly change, so a bit early to lock in timing,
but occasional rain chances look reasonable through the weekend.
Also, worth noting that the dry (rain-free) hours this weekend
should far out number the hours it is raining. 

There continue to be some signal in medium range guidance in a
more substantial shortwave moving bodily out into the central
Plains and then Mississippi Valley early next week. There is
considerable spread in the ensemble guidance in regards to
timing, track, and intensity of this system, but the idea of
additional chances of showers and thunderstorms early next week
looks reasonable. Temperatures early next week look to remain
above to much above average as warm air advection would likely
ramp up in advance of a more formidable shortwave. 

- Izzi
